title: Sahel drought and famine of 1972–1973
summary: Poor, badly distributed rains in 1972 and a poor 1973 rainy season brought drought across the Sahel, which a US State Department memorandum lists as Mauritania, Senegal, Mali, Upper Volta, Niger, Chad and the Gambia. One account estimates 100,000 to 200,000 people and as many as four million cattle died in 1972–1973; the memorandum said 20–25 million people faced starvation.

uncertainty.note: The State Department memo says world attention focused on the drought since the fall of 1972 and that the 1973 rainy season was also poor; EBSCO gives deaths for 1972-1973.

where.modern_name: Sahel region, West and Central Africa
where.historical_name: Sahelian West Africa: Mauritania, Senegal, Mali, Upper Volta, Niger, Chad and the Gambia (as named in the source)

importance.justification: A drought-driven famine across the Sahel that prompted international relief and later early-warning systems.

audience_note: Describes a famine with large loss of human life and livestock.

sources.title: Foreign Relations of the United States, 1969–1976, vol. E-6, doc. 20 (Sahel memorandum, 29 August 1974)
sources.publisher: Office of the Historian, US Department of State

reviewer_note: Death estimates differ across sources; I use only the EBSCO figure (100,000 to 200,000 people, as many as four million cattle). The 20-25 million figure is the memo count of people facing starvation, not deaths. Pin is the GeoNames Sahel centroid with wide uncertainty.
